title: CVE-2026-55607
summary: The vendor's advisory describes a sandbox escape: confusion over git worktree paths let code run outside the tool's sandbox. The failure is in how the tool resolves paths at the edge of its own sandbox, machinery the user never sees. A CVE and a vendor advisory were issued.

product: Claude Code, Goose, Hermes Agent, Qwen Code, Grok Build, OpenAI Codex, Cursor
title: GitSpawn
summary: Eight findings across seven command-line agents share one mechanism: while gathering context in the background, the agent runs git without neutralising the repository's own git configuration. A repository received as files, with its .git directory included, can therefore run code with the user's privileges, outside the sandbox, with no prompt and, on some agents, before any workspace question is shown.

title: PromptFiction
summary: A crafted app-launch link could deliver a prompt that the desktop app submitted without the user seeing or confirming it, with the harmful part hidden below harmless-looking text. Impacts named: exfiltration of conversation history and possible code execution where the app has file access. The fix makes such a prompt wait, pre-filled, until the user reads it and presses send.

title: DeepJack
summary: Two variants of a cursor:// deeplink open the MCP-install confirmation dialog with the server command partly out of view: the dialog shows it in a single-line field, so the user accepts a command they cannot fully read. Presented as a bypass of the fix for an older deeplink bug; the vendor closed the reports as duplicates.

title: CVE-2026-59726 (RufRoot)
summary: In the default docker-compose deployment, the MCP bridge endpoints were reachable without authentication. What followed: command execution in the bridge container, reading of provider API keys, and poisoning of the agent's learning store. Scored 10.0 by the CNA. No model is involved at any step.

title: CVE-2026-59950
summary: The deprecated WebSocket server transport in the official SDK accepted handshakes without validating the Host or Origin headers, the classic opening for cross-site WebSocket abuse. The patched version adds a validation setting that defaults to off.

product: MountDev AI MCP Connector for WordPress <= 1.6.1
title: CVE-2026-15015
summary: An unauthenticated attacker could obtain an administrator-bound OAuth bearer token by registering their own client and using an authorization endpoint that did not check who was asking. Scored 9.8 by the CNA.

title: GitLost
summary: Text planted in an issue on a public repository was followed by an agentic workflow that could read the organisation's repositories and write public comments; it published private repository content in a public comment. The configuration combined reading private data with writing in public.

product: Azure DevOps MCP server (tested with Copilot CLI and Claude Code)
title: Azure DevOps MCP confused deputy
summary: An instruction hidden in an invisible comment inside a pull-request description was acted on by the agent. The official server had a content-isolation defence applied to some tools, such as pipelines and wiki, but not to the tool that returns pull-request descriptions. Validated with two different agents; the vendor triaged the report.

title: Kiro workspace exfiltration
summary: Attacker-controlled workspace content, delivered through workspace settings and the IDE's Powers feature, could steer the agent into exfiltrating sensitive local data; it worked in both trusted and untrusted workspaces. Fixed by the vendor seven months before the research was published.
